title: Value Objects and Entities
summary: A value object is defined by its attributes and is immutable; an entity is defined by its identity and persists through change.
signals: a domain field typed as a bare string or number for something with a fixed set of legal states (status, type, kind)
a numeric amount with no attached currency or unit, or currency handled as a loose sibling field
equality that compares every field of an object that is supposed to have a durable identity
money-like arithmetic done with floats instead of integer minor units

roles.Order (before): entity smuggling business rules into primitive fields
roles.OrderStatus: value object: the legal states and the transitions allowed between them
roles.Money: value object: an immutable amount + currency, compared by value
roles.Order (after): entity: identity persists across attribute changes
roles.add_totals / Money.add: the operation that a value object can refuse when it doesn't make sense

stages.title: Primitives
stages.idea: Status and money are bare string/number fields, so nothing stops an invalid status or a cross-currency sum.

stages.title: Value objects and an entity
stages.idea: OrderStatus enforces legal transitions and Money enforces same-currency arithmetic; Order keeps identity-based equality.

checks: Why is comparing two Orders by id, not by all their fields, still correct even after the order's status changes?
Why does Money need to refuse cross-currency arithmetic instead of just adding the numbers?
What makes a type a value object rather than a primitive with the same fields?
Why do integer minor units avoid the float drift that plain floats have?
